---
title: "Questions and limits"
description: "Short answers about what OmicsBase is, where your code runs, what is sent to the model, R versions, packages and how to report a problem."
---

## How do I get help or report a problem? {#report-a-problem}

Open a public issue on GitHub: [github.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/issues](https://github.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/issues).

Say what you did, what you expected and what happened. If it happened in a note that holds nothing private, [share the note](share.qmd) and paste the link.

On a page of these docs, you can also use **Report an issue** in the page margin.

## What is OmicsBase? {#what-is-it}

OmicsBase is a free, open-source website for analysing microbiome, gene expression, single-cell, spatial, protein and metabolite data with R and Bioconductor.

It has two parts. In a **note**, the agent writes and runs R code for each question; see [Your first note](first-note.qmd). **Reports** runs an agent for bigger projects on the CSC Roihu supercomputer or on your computer; see [Reports on Roihu](reports-roihu.qmd).

## What is the agent set up for? {#what-it-is-not}

The agent is set up for data analysis in R and Bioconductor. Every number it reports comes from code that ran, and when data or a package is missing, it says so.

Read the code and check the results, as you would with any analysis.

## Where does my code run? {#where-code-runs}

On OmicsBase's servers at CSC in Finland. Each note has its own R session and folder.

You can also [run OmicsBase on your own computer](../self-host/install.qmd). Then notes run there.

## What is sent to the model provider? {#what-leaves-the-server}

The model runs at the company that provides it. In a note, that company receives:

- the messages you type,
- the code the agent writes,
- what R prints back, such as the first rows of a table,
- what the agent looks up in the Bioconductor books and the R help,
- the names of your files, and pictures and short documents you attach.

Data files you upload stay on OmicsBase's servers at CSC. The model sees only what R prints about them. See [What the model sees of your files](your-data.qmd#what-the-model-sees).

In Reports the agent works in your files directly, so whatever it opens, runs or prints goes to the provider of your key.

When a model comes through OpenRouter, OpenRouter passes each request to the company that runs the model. Each provider's terms decide how long it keeps what it receives and whether it trains on it. See [Choose a model](models.qmd).

Code and public data are fine to send. Personal data, such as patient records, should go only to a provider your organisation has approved for it.

## Which R and Bioconductor versions does it use? {#versions}

Bioconductor 3.24, with the R version that goes with it. To see the exact versions in a note, ask the agent: `Run sessionInfo()`. It lists R and every loaded package with its version.

## Which packages are installed? {#packages}

Over 200 R packages for omics analysis, plus the packages they depend on. They include mia, miaViz and miaTime for microbiome data, DESeq2, edgeR and limma for gene expression, scater for single-cell data, SpatialExperiment for spatial data, LimROTS, MaAsLin3 and ANCOM-BC for comparing groups, and data packages such as curatedMetagenomicData, MGnifyR, scRNAseq and STexampleData.

To check one package, ask the agent: `Is the package <name> installed?`

## Which tools can OmicsBase run? {#tools}

| Where | What it has |
| --- | --- |
| Notes | R and Bioconductor. Notes read the results of command-line tools, such as MetaPhlAn and Bracken profiles, BIOM files, count tables and Salmon output; the tools themselves run in Reports on Roihu. |
| Reports on Roihu | R and Bioconductor, plus about 300 command-line tools from CSC, such as fastp, Kraken 2, MetaPhlAn, bowtie2, SPAdes and GATK, and CSC's reference databases. |
| Reports on your own computer | R and Bioconductor only. |
| Local install | R and Bioconductor only, in notes and in Reports. |

To start from raw sequencing reads (FASTQ files), use Reports on Roihu, then bring the results to a note. [Bioinformatics tools on Roihu](reports-roihu.qmd#bio-tools) lists the tools.

## Can I install a package? {#install-packages}

Notes use the installed packages, and the agent's instructions keep it to them. If a package is missing, the agent says so and suggests an installed one that does the same job.

If you need a package that is missing, [open an issue](#report-a-problem) and name it.

## How long can a step run? {#time-limits}

A cell can use 10 minutes of R time; [The time limit](cells.qmd#time-limit) explains what counts and what to do when a step needs longer.

## How do I mention OmicsBase in a paper? {#cite}

Name OmicsBase and link to its code: [github.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase](https://github.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase). Also cite the R packages your analysis used. `sessionInfo()` lists them with their versions, and `citation("<package>")` in R gives the reference for each one.

## Is it free? {#cost}

Yes, to use at omicsbase.utu.fi. Models that OmicsBase pays for use a daily allowance of credits. If you use your own OpenRouter key, OpenRouter charges your account. See [Credits](models.qmd#credits).

## Can I use it without a University of Turku account? {#accounts}

Yes. You can sign in with a Google account. See [Sign in](first-note.qmd#sign-in).
